cards.title: What photosynthesis is
cards.explanation: Photosynthesis is how plants make their own food. They use energy from sunlight to turn water and carbon dioxide into a sugar called glucose. Oxygen is released as a by-product.
keyPoints: Plants make their food instead of eating it
Sunlight provides the energy
Glucose is the food and oxygen is the by-product
cards.rememberThis: Plants use light energy to turn water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.

cards.title: What plants take in
cards.explanation: Plants need three things for photosynthesis. Roots pull water up from the soil. Tiny holes in the leaves called stomata let carbon dioxide in from the air, and the leaves catch the sunlight.
keyPoints: Water comes in through the roots
Carbon dioxide enters through stomata in the leaves
Leaves catch the sunlight
cards.rememberThis: The inputs are water, carbon dioxide and light.

cards.title: Chlorophyll and chloroplasts
cards.explanation: Photosynthesis happens inside chloroplasts, small parts found in leaf cells. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, a green pigment that absorbs light. Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light best and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.
keyPoints: Chloroplasts are where photosynthesis happens
Chlorophyll is the pigment that absorbs light
Green light is reflected, so leaves look green
cards.rememberThis: Chlorophyll inside the chloroplasts captures the light energy.

cards.title: Light reactions
cards.explanation: The first stage needs light, so it is called the light-dependent reactions. Light energy splits water molecules apart. This releases oxygen and stores energy in two carrier molecules called ATP and NADPH.
keyPoints: Happens in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast
Water is split and oxygen is released
Energy is stored in ATP and NADPH
cards.rememberThis: The oxygen we breathe comes from water split during the light reactions.

cards.title: The Calvin cycle
cards.explanation: The second stage does not need light directly. It uses the energy stored in ATP and NADPH to turn carbon dioxide into glucose. This stage happens in the stroma, the fluid inside the chloroplast.
keyPoints: Also called the light-independent reactions
Carbon dioxide is fixed into sugar
Powered by ATP and NADPH from the light reactions
cards.rememberThis: The Calvin cycle builds glucose from carbon dioxide.

cards.title: What plants make
cards.explanation: The products of photosynthesis are glucose and oxygen. Plants burn glucose for energy and use it to build cellulose for their cell walls. Extra glucose is stored as starch for later.
keyPoints: Glucose gives the plant energy
Glucose builds cellulose and is stored as starch
Oxygen leaves the leaf through the stomata
cards.rememberThis: Carbon dioxide and water, with light, become glucose and oxygen.

cards.title: Why it matters for life on Earth
cards.explanation: Almost every food chain starts with photosynthesis, because plants are the producers that animals eat. Photosynthesis also puts oxygen into the air and takes carbon dioxide out. Without it, most life on Earth could not survive.
keyPoints: Plants are producers at the start of food chains
It adds oxygen to the air
It removes carbon dioxide from the air
cards.rememberThis: Photosynthesis feeds food chains and refills the air with oxygen.

cards.title: What changes the speed
cards.explanation: The rate of photosynthesis depends on light, carbon dioxide and temperature. Raising one speeds it up only until another runs short, and that one is called the limiting factor. Too much heat damages the enzymes, so the rate drops.
keyPoints: Brighter light speeds it up, up to a point
More carbon dioxide speeds it up, up to a point
Enzymes work best when warm, and heat damages them
cards.rememberThis: Light, carbon dioxide and temperature control how fast photosynthesis goes.

quiz.question: Through which part of the leaf does carbon dioxide enter?
quiz.explanation: Stomata are tiny holes in the leaf that let carbon dioxide in.

quiz.question: Why do most leaves look green?
quiz.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green, so we see green.

quiz.question: Where does the oxygen released by plants come from?
quiz.explanation: During the light reactions, water is split and its oxygen is released.

quiz.question: What does the Calvin cycle make?
quiz.explanation: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to turn carbon dioxide into glucose.

quiz.question: Why are plants called producers?
options: They make their own food from light
quiz.explanation: Plants make their own food, so food chains start with them.

quiz.question: A plant gets more light but its rate of photosynthesis stays the same. Why?
options: Another factor, like carbon dioxide, is now limiting
quiz.explanation: Once light is plentiful, the factor in shortest supply limits the rate.
